Project Summary – Space Analog Finder

Space Analog Finder is a web-based application developed to identify Earth locations that resemble potential permanent Moon base locations and regions on Mars. The application compares geographical and environmental characteristics such as slope, surface roughness, temperature conditions, and rockiness to find suitable Earth analogues. It includes interactive maps, location comparisons, similarity analysis, planetary region selection, and mission suitability dashboards. Users can select a Moon or Mars region and discover Earth locations with similar environmental characteristics through a ranking system. This project addresses the challenge of understanding and studying extraterrestrial environments by providing accessible Earth-based locations for research, simulation, and mission preparation. It is important because testing technologies, studying terrain, and preparing astronauts in Earth environments can support future lunar and Martian exploration. The application serves as an initial research and educational tool, with illustrative comparison data that can be improved using validated scientific datasets.
details:
Project Details – Space Analog Finder

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Space Analog Finder is a web-based application that identifies Earth locations with environmental and terrain characteristics similar to selected regions on the Moon and Mars. Users can select a planetary region, compare its characteristics with Earth locations, and view the closest matches through a similarity-ranking system. The application considers four major parameters: slope (30%), surface roughness (25%), thermal conditions (25%), and rockiness (20%). It presents the results using interactive maps, charts, comparison tables, and location profiles.

2. What are its benefits?

  • Helps researchers explore potential Earth-based analogue environments.
  • Supports educational studies of lunar and Martian exploration.
  • Makes planetary location comparison easier through visual analysis.
  • Provides a platform for preliminary research and mission preparation.

3. What is the intended impact?

The project aims to support future Moon and Mars exploration by helping identify Earth environments that can be studied as analogues. Such locations may be useful for terrain studies, equipment testing, research activities, and astronaut training.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

  • Programming language: Python
  • Framework: Streamlit
  • Data processing: Pandas
  • Mapping: Folium and Streamlit-Folium
  • Web technologies: HTML, CSS and JavaScript
  • Code editor: Visual Studio Code
  • Version control and code hosting: Git and GitHub

5. How is the project creative?

The project combines planetary exploration concepts with interactive web technology. Instead of simply displaying information about the Moon and Mars, it allows users to select regions, compare environmental parameters, discover ranked Earth analogues, and explore results visually in one application.

6. What factors did the team consider?

The main factors considered were terrain similarity, surface roughness, slope, temperature conditions, rockiness, ease of comparison, map accessibility, and the usefulness of the results for future planetary research. The application also considers usability by presenting complex comparisons through simple dashboards and visualizations.

Note: The current prototype uses illustrative comparison values. Scientific validation and reliable datasets are necessary before using its results for actual mission planning or site selection.
